observations: Predicted urgent10-minute job due10 is late if short5-minute job due30 runs first.
Short→urgent gave total waiting5 and one late job.
Urgent→short gave total waiting10 and zero late; target disabled at that ordering.
Reveal accurately compared five extra waiting minutes with zero lateness and limited the lesson to meeting due dates rather than minimizing waiting.
whyCool: The quick job can wait safely while the urgent one cannot.
caveat: Only two fixed jobs are tested; this is not a proof that earliest-deadline ordering minimizes the number of late jobs for arbitrary queues.
effort: Completed prediction, both orders, screenshot and reveal.
